correctness.rationale: The normalized Laurent polynomial identity gives the exact finite Fourier constant. The circle BV translation inequality proves the upper bound; the exact symmetric arc-leakage formula gives semicircle attainment, and BV coarea plus nested superlevel sets proves that all equality inputs are exactly two-level semicircle functions. Taylor expansion of the kernel at its antipode proves the parity orders and constants. Dominated convergence and the classical logarithmic integral establish the Jackson-square asymptotic. The included standard-library checker passed 968 exact coefficient and parity tests, positive quadrature and arc tests, plus large-degree asymptotic sanity checks. No finite test is used for an infinite quantifier.

originality.rationale: The 2010/2013 Nielsen treatment concerns matrix-weighted Lp convergence of Jackson summation, while the 2013 Babenko–Kryakin–Staszak article concerns continuous-function modulus inequalities and Jackson–Stechkin bounds. The 2024 Catala–Hockmann–Kunis–Wageringel paper uses the same squared-Fejér Jackson kernel to bound the first moment in Wasserstein measure approximation, so the kernel and its first-moment bound are prior art, but its inspected §§3.3–3.4 do not imply the exact BV-to-L1 norm, classification of all extremizers or the general powered parity-order law. An earlier published ordinary-Fejér q=1 BV claim establishes only the lower power case; it does not imply the explicit all-q finite constants or 2q+2 vanishing orders. Closest published-finding corpus hits concerning powered Fejér–Jackson kernels measure bounded-input-to-Lipschitz gain, a different norm. Unindexed older literature may contain equivalent formulas and cannot be excluded by these searches.
residual_risks: General positive-circle-convolution approximation principles and q=2 first moments have long antecedents; any separately stated historical BV equality theorem may have escaped index search.

value.rationale: Sharp error calibration on discontinuous periodic signals for the classical Jackson kernel and all integer-powered positive summation families is a natural approximation question. The exact finite-degree coefficient, full extremizer classification and parity-dependent high-order flatness provide information not supplied by known O(1/n) bounds; in particular raising power changes local robustness to displacement at even degrees from quartic to order 2q+2. q=2 asymptotic 6 log(2)/pi ties the natural Jackson rate to its sharp BV worst case. The isolated integral and elementary kernel identities are acknowledged as known and are not claimed as new.
